column1: # clang-spatch SmPL corpus manifest. One row per .cocci file.
# Corpora swept, all four in full, no sampling:
#   tier 1  every construct in the file is inside the subset: parse, compile, run.
#   tier 2  at least one live cocci rule is fully compilable and at least one
#           construct is not: compile the clean rules, name the rest, never apply
#           a rule whose pattern was only partly understood.
#   tier 3  no live cocci rule is compilable: refuse by name, produce no findings.
# Oracle classes: none=306, res-unverified=91, res-verified=760, res-verified + spatch-run=1, res-whitespace=27, spatch-run=24
#   res-verified    a .res checked in by Coccinelle's authors that this spatch
#                   reproduces byte for byte. Strongest evidence in the corpus.
#   res-unverified  a .res exists and this spatch does not reproduce it (the
#                   verdict is in the parentheses). Not usable as an oracle;
#   spatch-run      generated locally by harness/cocci-oracle.py, guarded by a
#                   hand-written positive control. Kernel rules only: the kernel
# oracle_status_counts is the per-file status histogram of the generated run.
#   HIT/CLEAN are results. NO_RULES means the patch has no -/+/* code and no
#   report script, so spatch says 'No rules apply' and exits 255: an empty
#   expectation by construction, not a clean file. SCRIPT_ERROR means a python
#   or ocaml script rule raised, which also exits 255. TIMEOUT, POISON and
#   In diff finding mode the column of a position is always 0, because a
#   unified diff carries line numbers only. Rules with a report script give
#   spatch version 1.3.3 compiled with OCaml version 4.14.1
#   Flags passed to the configure script: --enable-python --with-python=python3 --enable-opt --enable-ocaml
# How the spatch-run oracle was invoked, and why each guard is there:
#   one spatch process per C file, never --dir. Under --dir spatch prints
#   'EXN: Coccinelle_modules.Common.Timeout in fs/ntfs/mft.c', exits 0, and drops
#   that file with nothing in the output separating missing from empty; it also
#   merges several files into one HANDLING group and shares inferred typedefs
#   --timeout 90 always, because spatch defaults to no timeout: the same file
#   invoked directly runs for minutes instead of skipping.
#   the HANDLING: line that proves a file was analysed. api/atomic_as_refcounter
#   .cocci asks for --very-quiet in its own Options: line and the harness drops it.
#   Every run is refused unless a hand-written positive control fires first, so a
#   zero is a measurement. Controls are in c/kernel-controls/.
#   Python is enabled in this spatch (see the banner above); without it a rule
#   with a script:python report body finds nothing and exits 0.
# Limits of the tier and refusal columns: they come from a regex classifier
# (harness/smpl-refusals.py) reading the rules that are live in the mode named in
# the mode column, not from a SmPL parser. It resolves rule dependencies by
# satisfiability, so a rule guarded by 'depends on !<rulename>' counts as live.
# The 76 rows carrying a curated_id were also read by hand. The rest were not.
# 'virtual' and 'depends on' over virtuals are treated as inside the subset,
# following the scoping analysis, which counts them as base; the subset grammar
# document lists them as refusals. Without them no kernel rule reaches tier 1 or 2.
# All 118 cpptests rows are forced to tier 3: '#spatch --c++' selects the C++
# front end for the whole file and the subset's statement grammar is C.
